nodes.summary: The hypothesis CR₃^Inf is the following assertion. Let $d$ be a squarefree positive integer with $d\equiv5\pmod8$. Suppose that the 2-Selmer group $\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_d)$ has exactly $8$ elements and contains a pair $(a,b)$ with $|a|\equiv7\pmod8$. Then $y^2=x^3-d^2x$ has infinitely many rational solutions $(x,y)\in\mathbb Q^2$.

nodes.title: The class-number hypothesis in infinitely-many-points form

nodes.summary: The hypothesis CR₃^TYZ,Inf is the following assertion. Let $d$ be a squarefree positive integer with $d\equiv5\pmod8$ whose genus sum of row 5b, built from Rédei's bits, is odd: $T_{5b}(d)=1$. Then $y^2=x^3-d^2x$ has infinitely many rational solutions $(x,y)\in\mathbb Q^2$.
nodes.title: The Tian–Yuan–Zhang hypothesis in infinitely-many-points form

nodes.summary: The hypotheses CR₃^Inf and CR₃^Rk are equivalent. Likewise CR₃^TYZ,Inf is equivalent to CR₃^TYZ,Rk, CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Inf to CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk, and CR₃^DL,Inf to CR₃^DL,Rk.
nodes.title: The infinitely-many-points forms are equivalent to the positive-rank forms

nodes.summary: Let $d\ne0$ be a natural number and $C_d$ the curve $y^2=x^3-d^2x$ over $\mathbb Q$. Then $C_d(\mathbb Q)$ contains a point of infinite order if and only if $y^2=x^3-d^2x$ has infinitely many rational solutions $(x,y)\in\mathbb Q^2$.
nodes.title: A point of infinite order exists iff there are infinitely many rational points

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, the curve $y^2=x^3-d^2x$ has infinitely many rational points when the set of its affine rational solutions is infinite.
